Oral Judgment

These two appeals are filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 16.07.2014 in MVC.No.275/2012 and MVC.No.276/2012 passed by Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore, SCCH-14, for seeking enhancement of compensation and also for modification of liability fixed on respondent No.4-Owner of Toyota Qualis Car.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore, SCCH-14
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factum of accident and the injury sustained by the claimants are not in dispute.

The disputed fact in these cases is whether the insurer of Toyota Qualis Car, who is respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation or not is the question to be considered.
3. On 12.05.2010 at about 3.30 p.m., the claimants were travelling as passengers in Toyota Qualis Car bearing registration No.KA-03-MA-7010 and there was accident caused with lorry bearing registration No.TN-28-AB-9514, hence, the claimants sustained injuries.

The Tribunal has erred in holding that both drivers of the lorry and Toyota Qualis Car are equally responsible for causing the accident and accordingly, rashness NC: 2024:KHC:45517 and negligence was attributed at 50:50 ratio between the drivers of the lorry and Toyota Qualis car.
4. Upon consideration and re-appreciation of evidence, the finding arrived at by the Tribunal,
apportioning rashness and negligence at 50:50 is found to be correct, which needs no interference by this Court.
5. Considering the quantum of compensation awarded in both cases, the same are found to be just and proper, according to the nature of injuries sustained by the claimants.
Therefore, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal needs no interference by this Court.

But, the Tribunal has erred in holding that the owner of the Toyota Qualis Car- respondent No.4 is liable to pay the compensation, on the reason that the claimants are inmates of said Toyota Qualis Car.
Therefore, on this reason, the Tribunal held that the owner of Toyota Qualis Car is liable to pay the compensation by exonerating respondent No.3 insurer of the Car.
Admittedly, Ex-R2 is the Insurance policy of Toyota Qualis Car No.KA 03 MA 7010, which is a comprehensive/package policy.

Therefore, when the Insurance policy is comprehensive/package policy, NC: 2024:KHC:45517 then the risk of the inmates is also covered and there is no need to pay extra premium to cover the risk of inmates of the car.

This point is squarely covered by the judgment of this Court in the case of Divisional Manager,
United India Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Shamaraya and others in MFA No.31781/2010 and connected Sri Shivabalaswamy vs The United India Insurance Co Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101859577/

sentences.text: The Insurance policy-Ex-R2 was valid as on the date of the accident and since the insurance policy is a comprehensive/package policy, the third respondent-Insurer shall indemnify the owner of the Toyota Qualis car.
Accordingly, it is hereby directed that respondent No.3-The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., shall pay the compensation, to the claimants according to the apportionment fixed by the Tribunal.
6. Therefore, the finding recorded by the Tribunal on the aspect of liability is modified and the appeals filed by the claimants are liable to be allowed.

7. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
Appeals are allowed in part.
The judgment and award dated 16.07.2014 passed in MVC.No.275/2012 and MVC.No.276/2012 by Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore, SCCH-14 is hereby modified.
